history.takeaway: The market has had a long look at this home at about today's price, and no buyer has closed. That doesn't mean something is wrong with the house, but we need to know why the last contract fell apart before writing an offer.

offer_plan.posture_reason: Your lease ends soon and this is the floor plan you want, so the plan gives up some negotiating room to keep this home from going to another buyer.
offer_plan.conditions: the roof is documented as new, the failed contract fell through for reasons unrelated to the house, and no other offers are competing. If any of those changes, we'll revisit the numbers before you sign.

offer.heading: Negotiating Points
bullets: There is room to negotiate. The seller has cut the price four times, and has already lost one buyer. Mortgage rates are also higher now than when the earlier sales happened.
Seller help with closing costs is normal right now. Most recent sales in this area included seller-paid costs. Asking for a credit instead of a lower price can reduce the cash you need at closing.

Watch the appraisal. Only a few homes in Spring Oaks have sold above this home's price per square foot, all renovated pool homes. An offer near the top of the range raises the chance the appraisal comes in low, which you would have to cover in cash or renegotiate.

comps.method_note: Condition adjustments are based on listing descriptions, not visits, so they are judgment calls.

insurance.drivers: The main things that drive the cost for this house are the roof's age, the original construction (especially the wiring and plumbing), wind-mitigation features and the pool. Get a flood quote with the homeowners quote, and a real quote during your inspection period, after the four-point and wind-mitigation inspections.

credit_scenarios.takeaway: A credit is worth it if cash is tight or you might sell within a decade, and less so if you have savings to spare and plan to stay long term.

items: The roof. The first version of this listing described a brand-new roof. The current listing doesn't mention the roof at all. Roof age is the biggest factor in insuring a Florida home, so we want the permit and date in writing.
Why the last contract fell apart. If a previous buyer walked away over an inspection or appraisal problem, we want to know what it was.

Original wiring and plumbing. Homes of this era in Spring Oaks often have aluminum branch wiring and original cast-iron drains. Insurers ask about both. Add a sewer-line camera inspection to the general inspection.
Permits for the renovation. Confirm the kitchen, bath, and any electrical or plumbing work was permitted. Unpermitted work can cause problems with insurance and future resale.
The fourth bedroom. Check that the property appraiser's record shows four bedrooms, and if a room was converted, confirm it was permitted.
AC age and pool equipment. Neither is listed. Also confirm the pool has a compliant safety barrier.
"As-Is" doesn't mean no inspection. The As-Is contract still gives you an inspection period in which you can cancel for any reason. It only means the seller isn't committing to repairs.
